newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Mid-West power steady, ECAR rises on outage.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Mid-West power steady, ECAR rises on outage.

text.p: U.S. Midwestern bulk wholesale electricity prices were mostly steady Thursday, although prices in the East Central Area Reliability Coordination Agreement (ECAR) jumped higher on news of an outage in North Carolina, industry sources said.

Duke Power said its McGuire nuclear units 1 and 2 in Cornelius, N.C., with a total generation capacity of 2,258 megawatts, would be out of service for three to four weeks while a battery bank problem was corrected.

Duke's Oconee nuclear plant in Seneca, S.C., with a total generation capacity of 2,538 megawatts, has also been shut following an accident in September. No restart date has been set for the three Oconee units, but Duke has said they are not likely to come back in November.
The Duke outage had southeast traders looking to ECAR for electricity, and the tightening of supply pushed short-term prices higher, the brokers and marketers said.
Peak, non-firm electricity prices in ECAR for Friday delivery were assessed at $28.00-32.00 per megawatt hour (MWh) from next-day discussion at $18.00-19.00 on Wednesday.
Off-peak next-day ECAR power was difficult to find, but was notionally assessed unchanged at $12.50-14.00, the sources said.
November ECAR was being talked higher near $18.00 from $17.50-18.00 Wednesday, while December was pegged higher at $21.00-21.50 from $19.20-19.50 on Wednesday.
January/February ECAR was assessed at $21.50-21.75, the sources said.

In the Mid-Continent Area Power Pool (MAPP), peak non-firm power for Friday delivery was quoted higher at $19.00-21.00 with little business being done ahead of November 1 changes in power transmission regulations in MAPP, the sources said.
Off-peak non-firm MAPP power was said to have held steady at $10.00-11.50 per MWh.
In the Mid-American Interpool Network (MAIN), non-firm peak power was talked steady to higher at $23.00-26.50 from $20.00-24.00 on Wednesday, the brokers and marketers said.
Off-peak next day MAIN power was pegged steady at $12.00-14.00 per MWh.

Peak non-firm power prices in the Southwest Power Pool (SPP) were talked higher at $23.50-26.50 in the north from $20.00-24.00 on Wednesday, while southern SPP peak non-firm power was pegged at $27.00-29.00 from $25.00-28.00 on Wednesday.
Off-peak prices throughout SPP were reported to be steady at $12.00-16.00, the sources said.
Peak November SPP power was said to be talked at near $22.50 from Wednesday talk at $20.50-21.50, while December SPP was talked near $23.00 from $21.50-22.00 on Wednesday, the sources said.
-- Chris Reese, New York Power Desk 212-859-1627
